mike_infra: Heads up — starting ~02:10 UTC our ALB in us-west-2 began deregistering a bunch of edge-gpu targets in cluster-edge-2 (~180 target churn in 20m). Rolling 504s from the LB and sudden pod readiness flips. Anyone seeing this?

anna_sre: saw it too, noticed a big jump in conntrack count on edge nodes around the same time. ALB logs show health check timeouts (504/connection reset).

shuang: paste of alb logs? also any kube-proxy or iptables restarts?

mike_infra: grabbing logs now. ALB access log snippet: 
```
2026-03-18T02:12:03Z app/my-alb 10.0.5.43:443 10.0.100.17:30720 0.000 0.200 0.000 504 502 "GET /healthz HTTP/1.1" "ELB-HealthChecker/2.0" - - arn:aws:... 
```

mike_infra: kube-proxy on node-12 shows recent restart at 02:09. conntrack entries: `ss -s` looked like: 
```
TCP:   1024 (estab 900, closed 50, orphaned 0, synrecv 0, timewait 74/0),
Transport Total 120000
nf_conntrack: 128k used 116k
```

anna_sre: conntrack almost full. saw `nf_conntrack_max` at 131072. Many connections in TIME_WAIT/SYN_RECV from ALB ranges. Could be SNAT churn from service type or nodeport.

shuang: are these services using externalTrafficPolicy=Cluster? that causes SNAT and extra conntrack churn sometimes for large LB healthcheck fanout.

mike_infra: yes, our edge-gpu service is a NodePort Service w/ externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster (default). ALB targets are nodes (target type ip -> pods via hostNetwork/eni). Health checks fan out to lots of nodes.

sarah_prod: quick mitigation: can we patch svc to externalTrafficPolicy: Local for the gpu service? that should preserve source IP and avoid SNAT for LB traffic — reduces conntrack pressure. Downside: only nodes with endpoints serve traffic (but our fleet is pretty distributed).

anna_sre: also raising conntrack max and clearing stale entries helps short-term: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` and `conntrack -F` during low traffic window. Ops-bot: opening incident?

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-03018 created: "ALB health checks causing target churn — conntrack exhaustion". Severity: P2. Owners: eng-infra, eng-sre.

shuang: I can roll externalTrafficPolicy patch in a canary region. Plan: patch svc -> set Local, wait 2 health-check intervals, watch ALB target registration and conntrack on nodes with endpoints. If green, roll to rest.

mike_infra: +1. what's the health check interval/threshold? it's currently 10s interval, healthy threshold 2, unhealthy 2 — pretty aggressive. We can also increase the unhealthy threshold temporarily to reduce churn while we patch.

anna_sre: agree. I'll submit a quick patch to the k8s svc: 
```
kubectl patch svc edge-gpu -n edge --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/externalTrafficPolicy","value":"Local"}]'
```

anna_sre: Also bumped conntrack max on a couple of nodes for immediate relief: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=196608` — watching.

mike_infra: after the first canary change (node pool usw2-edge-a), ALB stopped deregistering targets for that AZ. conntrack used dropped ~40%. Nice.

sarah_prod: I'm seeing improvement on dashboards: target group healthy_count stable for canary nodes, overall 504s down 70%. Great.

shuang: roll complete to other AZs. Also filing upstream note: default Cluster mode + LB fanout -> conntrack pressure on nodes, recommend Local for services receiving LB healthchecks when possible.

anna_sre: follow-ups: 1) Longer term we should evaluate using IP target mode directly to podENIs (we already partly do this) and tighten ALB healthcheck settings (interval/healthy threshold) and 2) ensure our autoscaling replaces nodes with high conntrack burn instead of restarting kube-proxy.

mike_infra: opened ticket to AWS to validate ALB healthcheck fanout pattern and suggested we may need larger NLB/ALB capacity. Also added runbook step: if ALB target churn + kube-proxy restarts, check nf_conntrack, externalTrafficPolicy, and consider temporary unhealthy threshold bump.

shuang: adding note on tradeoffs: externalTrafficPolicy=Local will route LB traffic only to node-local endpoints — if endpoint distribution is uneven during upgrades/scale-downs we may see imbalance. Documented in runbook.

anna_sre: closing loop: incident reduced to monitoring after roll and conntrack bump. Leaving ticket open for AWS follow-up and runbook updates. :white_check_mark:

mike_infra: thanks team — good catch. If we see recurrence we'll re-open and consider more aggressive infra changes (bigger NAT, dedicated proxy, or moving health checks to fewer nodes).

sarah_prod: thumbs up. FYI: I notified product teams about transient 2–3 min blips earlier in the morning on affected clusters.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-03018 status changed to MONITORING.
